answer: Each epoch the network auctions a fixed number of working seats in a second-price clearing, and no agent may hold two. Buying a hundred seats means outbidding the marginal price on every one, so the clearing price the attacker pushes up multiplies across their whole block: total spend grows with the square of the clone count, while an honest single-seat member pays the same floor as always. A sybil farm funds its own opposition, climbing a trellis of rising costs toward a zenith it cannot afford, while the honest grove stays cheap to enter.
